# Getting `input()` from a user

In a lot of programs you write, you will want a user to give you some data to use.

The most fundamental way to do this in Python is with the `input()` function.

I will show you how to use this function live in class, because it will break the textbook build if I put `input()` in code cells. (If you are interested in why this happens, it is because the book runs the Python code, then it is converted to HTML, then sent to the website. When the Python code runs, if `input()` is in it, it will hang forever waiting for input, and the HTML will not build!).

The most basic way to use the `input()` function is just to use:

```
input()
```

When this code runs, an input box will appear. A user can type into this box.

Try this out in the cell below (the code is commented out so that the textbook build):

```{python}
# input()
input()
```

## Exercise - Getting User `input()` Data Validation Exercise

This exercise will get you to experiment with the `input()` function, and it will test your knowledge of comparison operators.

*Remember*: your [assignments, tests and exams](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_02_Class_Grades_Assignments_Exams.html) will also be a bit like this.

Click [here 🚀](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/pxr687/Intro_Comp_Programming/main?urlpath=tree/exercise_4b_input.ipynb) to launch the exercise on Binder.

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML
import numpy as np

roll = np.random.randint(1, 7)

message_text = f"""
<h2 style="color: green;">
🎲 The dice rolled a {roll}!
</h2>
"""

display(HTML(message_text))
```

import webbrowser
import tempfile

roll = np.random.randint(1, 7)

bet = input('Make your bet!:')

if roll == bet:
    emoji = ":)"
else:
    emoji = ":("

message_text = f"""
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
<h1 style="color: green;">
🎲 Dice Roll
</h1>
<p style="color: red;">
The dice rolled a {roll}.
</p>
<p style="color: green;">
You bet it would roll {bet}.
Your bet is {bet == roll} {emoji}
</p>
</body>
</html>
"""

display(HTML(message_text))
